fact.en: Trap 1: Protostar Energy Source: Protostars do NOT generate energy through nuclear fusion. A common trap is saying they fuse hydrogen. They shine due to gravitational contraction (releasing gravitational potential energy as thermal heat). Fusion only begins in the Main Sequence phase.
fact.hi: Trap 1: Protostar Energy Source: Protostars do NOT generate energy through nuclear fusion. A common trap is saying they fuse hydrogen. They shine due to gravitational contraction (releasing gravitational potential energy as thermal heat). Fusion only begins in the Main Sequence phase.

fact.en: Trap 2: Heavy Element Synthesis: Stars can only fuse elements up to Iron (Fe) in their cores. Fusing iron absorbs energy (endothermic) rather than releasing it, which triggers immediate core collapse. All elements heavier than iron (like gold, lead, and uranium) are synthesized during supernova explosions or neutron star mergers.
fact.hi: Trap 2: Heavy Element Synthesis: Stars can only fuse elements up to Iron (Fe) in their cores. Fusing iron absorbs energy (endothermic) rather than releasing it, which triggers immediate core collapse. All elements heavier than iron (like gold, lead, and uranium) are synthesized during supernova explosions or neutron star mergers.

fact.en: Trap 3: Chandrasekhar Limit Context: The Chandrasekhar Limit ($1.44 M_\odot$) applies to the mass of the degenerate core remnant (white dwarf), not the starting birth mass of the star. A star born with 6-8 solar masses can end up as a white dwarf if it sheds enough mass during its red giant phase.
fact.hi: Trap 3: Chandrasekhar Limit Context: The Chandrasekhar Limit ($1.44 M_\odot$) applies to the mass of the degenerate core remnant (white dwarf), not the starting birth mass of the star. A star born with 6-8 solar masses can end up as a white dwarf if it sheds enough mass during its red giant phase.

fact.en: Trap 4: Our Sun's End: Our Sun will NOT end in a supernova. Due to its low mass, it will gently shed its outer layers as a planetary nebula, leaving behind a carbon-oxygen white dwarf.
